en: Praise for the Ritual Service for Reciting Sutras, Walking the Path, and Vowing to Be Reborn in the Pure Land, Volume One,
Compiled and Recorded by the Śramaṇa Shandao.
I reverently invite the Four Heavenly Kings to enter directly into the site of practice;
I reverently invite the Lion King, whose majestic form is difficult even for lions to encounter.
With his powerful body and shaggy mane, he causes all demons to retreat and disperse.
Turning back, I request the Dharma Master to lead me directly to the City of Nirvana.
Preface: I humbly observe that this Sahā world is a vast and boundless house on fire.
The six realms of existence surround us like a realm of profound darkness and eternal night;
born blind and sightless, the light of wisdom has not yet dawned.
Without a means to guide them, all together are crushed in the land of death.
Cycling through coming and going like the long-flowing current of a river,
who can save those who entrust their lives and souls to it?
This is because sentient beings are infinite in number.
The kalpas since the exhaustion of all dust have further passed;
from that time until now, how many days have elapsed in this long wandering before encountering a superior condition?
From the primordial limit of Tathāgata Sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijña upward, [this has been so].
Thus, down to the present time, all the Śākyamuni Buddhas have relied upon the simultaneous practice of great vows and compassionate wisdom,
never abandoning sentient beings as they universally transform them through the three wheels of activity.
However, my veil of ignorance is heavy;
I did not encounter the Buddha when he appeared in the world.
Even had I been born at the same time as him, [I would still have failed].
It is like an overturned vessel;
divine light shines equally upon all, making no distinction among the four modes of birth,
and its compassion is impartial, benefiting all through the nourishment of the Dharma.
Although I have been submerged in the waters of the Dharma for long kalpas, I remain stubborn;
as suffering and its accumulation cause one another, the poisonous fire now breaks out within me.
Looking up, I contemplate your great compassion and profound kindness, which equally moisten the field of my body.
Through the secret empowerment of wisdom, the sprouts of the Way flourish;
with compassion and skillful means, he observes and instructs according to what is appropriate,
exhorting others to mind Amitābha and return to the Pure Land.
The ground is interspersed with various treasures, their radiance vying in brilliance;
the waters of virtue are clear and lustrous, their reflections penetrating and transparent;
jeweled towers rise in successive tiers, equaling the splendor of divine light.
The forest trees hang with garlands, and the wind carries elegant melodies;
the flower terraces are resplendent and pure, filled with all manner of wonders.
The noble assembly dwells together there, their brilliance surpassing that of a thousand suns.
His body is the color of purple-gold, with the marks and signs of excellence solemnly manifest;
in his coming and going, he traverses space without obstruction.
As for his environment of dependent retribution, it transcends the ten directions.
The earth, space, and all else are entirely without distinction.
Ordinary beings and sages from other directions travel to and fro by virtue of their vows;
upon arriving there, they are no different from one another, being equal and non-retrogressive.
The Tathāgata, employing skillful means, exhorts all four modes of birth in general to abandon this Sahā world and aspire to birth in Sukhāvatī;
they should single-mindedly recite the Buddha’s name while concurrently chanting the Amitābha Sūtra.
Desiring to cause them to recognize those adornments and to weary of these miserable affairs,
one takes life as the limit for the completion of the three causes and five recollections;
through the four cultivations of the primary and auxiliary practices, there shall be no interval even for a single kṣaṇa.
May these meritorious deeds universally benefit all sentient beings.
When their lives come to an end, may they ascend the celestial platform and together reach that land.
For those who wish to establish a site of practice for themselves or for others:
First, one must adorn the hall and install the sacred images.
Whether the banners and flowers are many or few, all members of the assembly should be made to bathe,
don clean robes, and enter the *maṇḍala* to listen to the Dharma.
If one wishes to summon people and those who offer praise and harmony, all should stand;
let the great assembly sit down.
First, have one person burn incense and scatter flowers, completing a single circuit around the perimeter.
Then, according to the ritual, perform the invocation with these words:

"May we be born into the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi! The great assembly, with one mind, weary of the immeasurable pleasures of the three realms, Aspires to be born into the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi!
May the three evil paths be forever severed, and may we attain the immeasurable bliss that is beyond naming!"

The triple world is a burning house difficult to dwell in; I vow to be reborn there. Riding upon the power of the Buddha’s vows, I go to the West to the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi;
I vow to be reborn there. Mindful of repaying the kindness of my parents, I always wear the Buddha upon my crown in immeasurable bliss;
the great assembly stands with flowers in hand in reverent devotion, vowing to be reborn there. First, I invite Amitābha to enter the Dharma hall in immeasurable bliss.
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: May I vow to be reborn there; Not failing his great vow, he shall welcome me at the appointed time. The Joy of Immeasurable Adornment:

May I vow to be reborn among the hosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges who take Amitāyus as their object of contemplation; Riding upon the lotus flowers of the Buddha-vehicle, they come to enter the assembly.
The Joy of Immeasurable Bliss: May I vow to be reborn there; Avalokiteśvara takes my hand and leads me into the lotus calyx. The Joy of Immeasurable Bliss.
May I be reborn through the vow of Śākyamuni Buddha, who is adorned with unsurpassed majesty; may I receive my humble heart’s wish and enter the place of practice for immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn in the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi. May I shatter my body in repentance for the immeasurable kindness of Śākyamuni;
may I be reborn among the great assembly in that land of ocean-like adornment for immeasurable bliss. May I follow the Buddha upon a flower and come to this assembly for immeasurable bliss.
The joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, the vow to be reborn there— The immeasurable joy of assisting the Buddha’s divine transformations to deliver sentient beings.

The Buddhas of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, extend their tongues and vow for rebirth there— May I, an ordinary being, realize birth in peace and bliss, the immeasurable joy.
The joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, the vow to be reborn there— The immeasurable joy of the compassionate mind that benefits all things, the great compassionate mind.

With shame and remorse, and with a great compassionate heart vast as the sands of the Ganges, I vow to be reborn there; Accepting my humble mind, may I enter the Dharma-assembly and enjoy immeasurable bliss—the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi—I vow to be reborn there.
With single-minded devotion, I look forward to the Pure Land and the Buddha’s presence, enjoying immeasurable bliss;

Together with the ocean-like assemblies of each and every Tathāgata, I vow to be reborn there; Riding upon the Buddha’s vehicle and arriving on lotus flowers to enter the assembly, I shall enjoy immeasurable bliss.
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: May I vow to be born there—this is the supreme condition for birth, a joy of immeasurable extent.
The Buddhas have sent twenty-five bodhisattvas to wish for my birth there; at all times they come to constantly protect and mind me—a joy of immeasurable extent.
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: May I vow to be born there—until the end of life, I shall enter directly into the city of Nirvāṇa—a joy of immeasurable extent.
The Buddha fears that sentient beings may encounter the four māras and obstruct their vow for rebirth;
until reaching the Land of Ultimate Bliss, they might fall into the three miserable realms—through the joy of immeasurable bliss and the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, I vow to be reborn there.

With a straightforward mind and true practice, the Buddha comes to welcome us—through this immeasurable joy, I and the assembly now offer our profound apologies and vow to be reborn there. Accepting our humble sincerity, come to enter this assembly—through this immeasurable joy.

The bliss of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*—may I vow to be born there. With every thought focused intently, may I leave the Sahā world for the immeasurable bliss of my own land, where Amitābha and the assembly of sages dwell;
may I vow to be born there. May they all come together in equality to sit at the site of enlightenment;
the bliss of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*—may I vow to be born there. The holy assembly at the site of enlightenment is truly difficult to encounter; it is immeasurable bliss.

May the assembly prostrate to the Amitābha Assembly and vow to be reborn there; may they universally scatter incense and flowers as an offering, and vow to be reborn in the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi.
May the light of Amitābha gather those who seek rebirth, and may they vow to be reborn in the immeasurable bliss of facing the Buddha Amitābha at the Nirvāṇa Assembly.
May each person make a vow and request a lotus pedestal, and vow to be reborn in immeasurable bliss.
Through the bliss of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*, I vow to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, where the gates of adornment are all wide open;
through immeasurable bliss, may I be born by the bliss of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*. With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, one sits upon a lotus pedestal;
through immeasurable bliss, may I be born by the bliss of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*. Riding upon the flower, enter directly without doubt; through immeasurable bliss.
May the assembly with one mind pray for the joy of rebirth upon the high seat;
may the compassionate and wise Zhìyǐng preach this sublime sutra of the inconceivable joy of rebirth. The joy of rebirth beneath the twin śāla trees;
the joy of inconceivable rebirth at the site of enlightenment, a time so difficult to encounter; the joy of rebirth when impermanence is swift and life cannot be stayed.
The inconceivable joy of rebirth; The joy of rebirth beneath the twin trees;
The inconceivable joy of rebirth, seen by all before their eyes as they follow the path of karma. All arise from the causes and conditions of the three poisons.
The inconceivable joy of rebirth; The joy of rebirth beneath the twin trees; The inconceivable joy of rebirth.
Though having obtained a human body, one is always dull-witted; this is the joy of rebirth. Craving, hatred, and false views become ever more intense;
this is the inconceivable joy of rebirth, the joy of rebirth beneath the twin trees.

This is the inconceivable joy of rebirth, the joy of rebirth where day and night one remains in a state of stupor without awakening; it is still the cause for wandering through the three miserable realms—this is the joy of rebirth.
The inconceivable joy of rebirth; The joy of rebirth beneath the twin trees;
The inconceivable joy of rebirth, suddenly ending the suffering of long kalpas in saṃsāra; When shall we hear of the joy of rebirth in Amitābha’s Pure Land?
The inconceivable joy of rebirth; The joy of rebirth beneath the twin trees; The inconceivable joy of rebirth.
The joy of the great assembly with one heart requesting the high seat for rebirth; The inconceivable joy of turning the wheel of Dharma to deliver all sentient beings;
The joy of rebirth beneath the twin *śāla* trees; The joy of inconceivable rebirth;
The joy of the multitude inclining their hearts to hear the Dharma; The joy of constantly making offerings with hands holding incense and flowers.
The inconceivable joy of rebirth; the joy of rebirth beneath the twin trees;

the inconceivable joy of rebirth at the site of enlightenment—within the great assembly, we together pay homage with a sincere heart. Namo to the eternally abiding Buddha and the great assembly at the site of enlightenment;
within the great assembly, we together pay homage with a sincere heart. Namo to the eternally abiding Dharma.
The assembly at the site of enlightenment, joining together with a sincere heart, pays respectful homage: Namo to the eternally abiding Sangha.
I respectfully address the assembly at the site of enlightenment: each of you should now collect and compose your minds.
Clapping their hands, joining their palms, and prostrating with their heads to the ground, they take refuge.
They pay homage to the Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha and to all World-Honored Ones of the past, present, and future.
As for the reason for taking refuge in the Buddha:
The Buddha is the great compassionate father of all sentient beings;
he is also a supreme and auspicious condition for transcending the world.
When one calculates his benevolence and virtue, [they are beyond measure].
Even if one were to describe them for more than a kalpa of dust, it would be impossible to exhaustively recount them.
The *Sūtra of the Wise and the Foolish* states:
"Each and every Buddha..."
From the first aspiration until the attainment of Bodhi,
they single-mindedly seek the Dharma without regard for body or wealth;
practicing both compassion and wisdom together, they never harbor a thought of retreat.
Some encountered people who forced them to undergo the dismemberment of their skin and flesh;
some cut their own bodies to prolong the lives of pigeons;
and some sacrificed a thousand heads in their quest for the Dharma.
Some drove a thousand nails into their bodies to seek four lines of verse;
some pierced their own flesh to provide blood for yakṣas;
and some abandoned their wives and children to satisfy rākṣasas.
Alternatively, employing compassionate skillful means,
he may manifest as birds or fish to provide relief for the common people and spare them from the hardships of hunger.
Sometimes he transforms himself into a golden-haired lion to protect hunters;
sometimes he becomes a white elephant and extracts its tusks to offer as a gift for the sake of seeking Bodhi;
and sometimes he regards his enemies as if they were his own infants.
Or he may manifest as an outsider, treating them like his own children;
since there is no difference between him and them, what distinction can there be between the sage and the ordinary person?
Throughout the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* of practice,
all actions are associated with the untainted (*anāsrava*).
Only when the merit is fully realized stage by stage is the fruit perfected, and one is designated a Buddha.
His body was the color of Jambu-river gold,
like a thousand suns vying for brilliance;
his marks and signs were distinct and clear, like the many stars in a bright night sky.
Seated upright in the full lotus posture, his countenance was perfectly clear and radiant;
the entire dharma-realm returned to a single source,
and each beheld the Tathāgata’s facial features.
Body and mind are profoundly tranquil;
yet their transformative activity never misses the opportune moment,
adapting and transforming according to the capacities of beings.
The substance of the retribution is fundamentally unmoving;
it is simply that the Tathāgata’s wisdom and virtue are so vast as to be difficult to exhaust in praise.
Thereupon, the assembly at the site of enlightenment each gave rise to a heart of shame and gratitude.
He was able to cause all the Buddhas to relinquish their bodies for my sake across kalpas as numerous as dust motes.
How lamentable it is that the World-Honored One is capable of such a difficult feat!
For long kalpas, he diligently endured the suffering of fatigue and pain;
though he performed ascetic practices for the sake of others' birth [into higher realms],
he did not seek even the slightest personal benefit.
May they aspire to transcend worldly toil and afflictions, realize Bodhi, and return to the other shore.
May the assembly with one mind act for the sake of the current patrons, such-and-such individuals.
We respectfully invoke all the World-Honored Buddhas of the ten directions.
As for us disciples, we reverently seek the realm of the Buddhas;
only the Buddhas can know it.
The essence of these lands is beyond the measure of ordinary beings;
the transformative functions of the three bodies all establish pure lands to guide all living beings.
The essence of the Dharma is without distinction;
those with consciousness who take refuge in it attain awakening.
It is only because ordinary beings harbor distracted thoughts that they have no means of entrusting themselves to it.
May all the Śākyamuni Buddhas not abandon their compassion,
but directly point toward the Western direction, ten trillion lands away,
where the land is named Sukhāvatī and the Buddha is titled Amitābha.
He now preaches the Dharma.
That land is pure, adorned with the four virtues;
it is forever free from reproach and devoid of sorrow or affliction.
Whether human or celestial, good or evil, all shall attain rebirth there;
upon arrival, they will be indistinguishable from one another, equal and uniform, and none shall fall back. Why is this so?
It was at the stage of his causal ground, under the Buddha Śikhin (World-Raorāja), that Amitābha relinquished his royal position and left the household life.
Thereupon, he gave rise to the mind of compassion and wisdom and extensively propagated the Forty-Eight Vows.
By the power of these Buddha-vows, even those who have committed the five heinous crimes and the ten evil deeds can extinguish their offenses and attain birth [in the Pure Land].
Even those icchantikas who slander the Dharma will all go there once they turn their hearts back [to the path].
Furthermore, due to the request made by Vaidehī, he vowed to abandon the Sahā world;
with every thought and without exception, he resolved to seek rebirth in Sukhāvatī.
In response to this request,
the Tathāgata immediately expounded the two gates of concentration and dispersion, as well as the three blessings and nine chapters,
extensively providing benefit for those who had not yet heard them.
The Buddhas of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
together praise Śākyamuni;
he extends his tongue so that it completely covers the three thousandfold world system.
It is not erroneous that one attains rebirth [in the Pure Land].
Thus, these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
do not abandon their compassion.
I accept the invitation of the present patron [Name] and all sentient beings to enter this maṇḍala to witness and certify their merit.
Having thus made the formal invitation:
Now, I exhort all sentient beings to each collect their minds, take refuge, and join their palms.
Descending from the seat, he receives those above and praises them, saying:
"May you be reborn! May you be reborn!"
May the assembly all take refuge in our original teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha, and in all the Tathāgatas of the worlds of the ten directions.
We pray that you will accept the invitation of these donors and sentient beings,
and, not forsaking your compassion, enter this maṇḍala.
It is proven that merit extinguishes all transgressions;
with a single thought of turning the mind, one beholds Amitābha.
May the bodies and minds of the assembly all leap with joy.
Holding incense and flowers in hand, one constantly makes offerings.
[The Invocation for High and Low Recipients] says: "High and low, please descend. [The Request for Invitation] says:
"I respectfully address you once more."
The great assembly at the site of enlightenment each gathered their minds,
snapped their fingers, and joined their palms;
bowing their heads, they single-mindedly took refuge.
For the sake of the present donor and all sentient beings,
one should next respectfully invite the eighty-four thousand *sūtra* treasuries spoken by the Buddhas of the ten directions and the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*),
as well as the bodily relics and dispersed relics.
I only pray that you will emit great divine light to enter this place of practice and bear witness to these meritorious virtues.
Furthermore, I invite the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and noble sages who have attained the Way from the ten directions;
I only pray that you will not forsake your compassion and manifest great supernormal powers.
Entering this maṇḍala, one realizes and witnesses its merit.
Furthermore, one should respectfully invite the assembly of bodhisattvas, including Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and pray:
"We only beseech you not to abandon your compassion, but to fulfill the vows of all sentient beings."
Entering this maṇḍala to witness and certify their meritorious virtues,
the reason for taking refuge and making this invocation is that these bodhisattvas,
from their first aspiration until they reach bodhi, [have cultivated these qualities].
He constantly acts with impartiality in guiding others without bias;
he never ceases for even a moment in benefiting himself and others;
and he perpetually awakens all the worlds with the sound of the Dharma.
Its radiance universally illumines immeasurable Buddha-lands;
all worlds tremble in six ways,
completely encompassing the realm of Māra and shaking his palaces.
Tearing asunder the nets of heterodoxy and extinguishing all views;
dispersing the dust of afflictions and destroying the moats of desire;
opening wide and elucidating the gates of the Dharma.
Manifesting the pure, clear, and radiant fusion of the Buddha-dharma,
they propagate the true transformation and constantly perform untainted actions of body, speech, and mind.
They constantly practice non-retrogressive conduct of body, speech, and mind;
they constantly practice unshakable karma of body, speech, and mind;
and they constantly practice praiseworthy karma of body, speech, and mind.
He constantly practices pure actions of body, speech, and mind;
he constantly practices actions of body, speech, and mind free from affliction;
he constantly practices actions of body, speech, and mind characterized by wisdom.
Having attained awakening and perfected both meditative concentration and wisdom,
these bodhisattvas are constantly attended by the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, human kings, Brahmā kings, and others.
They shall guard, revere, and make offerings [to them].
For all sentient beings, they shall be a rescue, a refuge, an illumination,
a venerable one, a supreme one, and a preeminent one.
Possessing immeasurable practices and vows, he brings great benefit;
he establishes gods and humans in peace and security, benefiting all beings.
He wanders through the ten directions, employing skillful means and expedients.
They enter the treasury of the Buddha-dharma and reach the ultimate further shore;
their wisdom and holy brilliance are inconceivable as they turn the wheel of the Buddha’s Dharma.
They have accomplished the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes and have attained complete mastery over all phenomena.
Such bodhisattva mahāsattvas as these are beyond measure or calculation.
I only pray that you will not forsake your compassion;
please accept the invitation of sentient beings and come together at once to enter this dharma-assembly,
acting as a witness to the merit of the current patron, [Name].
Now, I exhort the assembly at the site of enlightenment and all others present:
compose your minds, take refuge, join your palms, and pay homage.
Following this, recite the high praise as follows:
May we be reborn there; may we be reborn there.
May the assembly long to hear the teachings of all Buddhas within the eighty-four thousand treasuries of the Dragon Palace.
Having already bestowed divine light upon entering the place of practice,
they witness their merit and fulfill their vows;
through this, they leave suffering behind and behold Amitābha.
The sentient beings within the Dharma-realm likewise have their obstructions removed;
our bodies and minds all leap with joy,
as we constantly make offerings with hands holding incense and flowers.
Gao responded with a chant:
"May we be reborn there! May we be reborn there!
The sutra treasuries in the Dragon Palace are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges."
The Buddhadharma of the ten directions exceeds even this;
I now direct my mind to universally invite them all to emit great divine light and enter the site of enlightenment.
To verify their merit and further eliminate their transgressions,
and to increase the sprouts of bodhicitta in the donors,
may all members of the assembly each recite with a unified mind.
Holding incense and flowers in hand, constantly making offerings;
following this, recite the high praise:
"May I be reborn there! May I be reborn there!"
Today this place of practice is difficult to encounter;
the unsurpassed Buddha-dharma is likewise difficult to hear.
Until the end of life, though my body may wither away, I shall sever all evils.
From this moment on, every thought-moment shall eradicate all transgressions;
the six sense faculties shall attain true awakening.
Through precepts, meditative concentration, and compassion, my vows shall never be in vain.
The assembly’s bodies and minds all leaped with joy;
holding incense and flowers in their hands, they constantly made offerings.
[High ones] spoke in praise of those below, and [those below] spoke in praise of those above.
May I be reborn there; may I be reborn there.
May I dwell long in the Sahā world, forever putting an end to the constant sinking of all beings in the three evil realms and the four modes of existence.
Covered in fur and bearing horns, they undergo manifold sufferings;
they have never heard or seen the name of a Noble One.
Recalling these matters of exhaustion throughout long kalpas.
Vowing to cast off this life to behold Amitābha,
the assembly’s bodies and minds all leaped with joy;
holding incense and flowers in their hands, they constantly made offerings.
The Abbot received the response with praise, saying:
"May you all attain rebirth! May you all attain rebirth!
Then the assembly together took refuge.
Now, for the sake of the donors and all sentient beings,
we have invited the entire-body śarīras and the vajra-fragmented śarīras of the Buddhas throughout the ten directions and the Dharma-realm;
may their merit and benefits be bestowed as appropriate.
The forms divide and the shadows follow;
although the divided forms differ in size,
their spiritual transformations are of one kind and no different.
On a large scale, they are comparable to mountains;
on a small scale, they are likened to mustard seeds or motes of dust.
They dedicate their lives with sincere devotion, unifying their hearts in making offerings.
In the near term, humans and devas obtain rewards;
wealth and joy accompany them for long kalpas.
In the distant term, they attain the fruit of non-arising in the Pure Land.
Thus, may there be the eternal bliss of Nirvana.
Furthermore, I pray that the assembly at this site of enlightenment will each align their hearts with one accord.
Holding incense and flowers in hand, they constantly make offerings.
Following this, they join their voices in high praise, saying:
"May we be reborn there! May we be reborn there!"
Whether the relics of the True Body are large or small,
those who see or hear of them will rejoice and cultivate offerings;
this becomes their own roots of goodness and a source of merit for others.
I dedicate all gathered merits;
with diligent effort day and night, I dare not retreat.
With single-minded resolve, I shall behold Amitābha.
The assembly, both body and mind, were filled with joy;
holding incense and flowers in their hands, they constantly made offerings.
[High ones] spoke in praise of those below; [those below] spoke in praise of those above.
May I be reborn there; may I be reborn there.
Such are the great vows of Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī;
so too are those of all the children of the Buddhas throughout the ten directions.
In a single thought, my emanations pervade the six realms;
according to their capacities, I transform and deliver them, severing the bonds of cause and condition.
May I, in birth after birth, attain close proximity to you.
Surrounding [the teacher] to listen to the Dharma and awaken to the gate of truth,
may we forever uproot the karma of ignorance and birth-and-death;
we vow to become inhabitants of Amitābha’s Pure Land.
May the assembly each bring body and mind into alignment;
holding incense and flowers in their hands, they constantly make offerings.
[The following connects with the high praise:]
I vow to be reborn there; I vow to be reborn there.
The Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, with great compassion, do not spare their own bodies or lives as they deliver sentient beings.
Manifesting as emanations throughout the six realms according to their kind,
you preach the sublime Dharma so they may realize non-arising.
Within the pure land of non-arising, you enter alongside all beings.
Vast, expansive, and beyond measure,
he constantly beholds the Buddha through his fourfold majestic deportment;
accompanied by his dharma companions, he enters the precious hall.
The assembly, both body and mind, were filled with joy;
holding incense and flowers in their hands, they constantly made offerings.
[The lower section] follows the high praise, while [the high section] follows the lower praise.
May there be rebirth; may there be rebirth.
For the sake of the present patron and all sentient beings, we respectfully invite the worthy sages and holy ones to enter the ritual arena.
By proving these merits and practicing offerings,
the afflictions of the three poisons are thereby extinguished;
the darkness of ignorance and all transgressions are entirely removed.
May I encounter all Buddhas in every birth,
and in every thought-moment cultivate the path until reaching the state of no-remainder;
may I dedicate the merit and karma of this present life [to that end].
In the future, he will certainly abide in the Golden Canal;
may all of you, with body and mind in perfect harmony,
hold fragrant flowers in your hands and offer them constantly.
Following this, he recites the high praise:
"Vow to be reborn! Vow to be reborn!
Though the bodies of the Bodhisattvas and the Holy Assembly differ,"
Their compassion and wisdom are equal and without distinction;
they do not spare body or wealth in their quest for the sublime Dharma,
never ceasing even in the face of difficult practices and austerities.
I vow to reach Bodhi and ascend to the other shore;
emitting great compassion, I shall ferry those in the stream of existence across.
The beings in the stream of existence are my very own body.
Riding upon the light, they complete their lives and enter the Western Land;
the assembly’s body and mind are all filled with exultation,
holding incense and flowers in their hands to offer constant worship.
The High-ranking official responds with a praise, saying: "May there be rebirth! May there be rebirth! The Lower-ranking official responds with a praise, saying:
"For the sake of the current patrons, we have already invited all Buddhas of the ten directions into this ritual arena."
The true śarīra from the Dharma-treasury of the Dragon Palace has already emitted divine light into the site of enlightenment;
Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas possess sovereign mastery of the supernormal powers.
